title: praxis hook manifest
description: Structural schema for hooks/manifest.json, the canonical hook registry (ADR-0001 §2.5). Every object level is closed (additionalProperties: false) so a typo'd optional key fails validation instead of being silently absorbed. Validated by the stdlib walker in scripts/check-plugin-manifests.py — that walker supports only the keywords this file uses (type, enum, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, minimum, minItems, minLength); extend the walker before introducing a new keyword here.

dispatch_groups.description: (event, matcher) pairs collapsed into a single dispatcher node per platform hooks.json (ADR-0002). Non-tool events (Stop, SubagentStop, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit) carry no matcher: OMIT the key rather than setting it null — the validator subset has no null type, and .get('matcher') yields None for an absent key anyway (issue #1199 review).

hooks.description: Flat, order-significant hook registrations. A multi-event hook appears once per (event, matcher) registration under the same name.

role.description: One of the four ADR-0001 role directories (mirrors VALID_ROLES in scripts/constants.py).

event.description: Host lifecycle event. PostToolUseFailure and SubagentStop (#1337) are documented for Claude Code only — a registration on either carries hosts: ["claude"]. PostToolUseFailure is a per-hook event, so the dispatch_groups enum above does not list it; SubagentStop shares Stop's decision format and does have a group.

matcher.description: Tool-name regex for PreToolUse/PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure registrations, or a SessionStart source (startup|resume|clear|compact|fork — postcompact-context uses `compact`, #1339); omitted for the other non-tool events.

body.description: Present iff the shell file IS the hook body (not a generated wrapper). The build treats any other value as impl.py, so the value set is closed.

args.description: Extra argv for the hook command. With wrapper_suffix set, baked into the wrapper body; otherwise appended to the hooks.json command line.

wrapper_suffix.description: Per-event wrapper filename suffix for multi-event Python hooks (hooks/<name><suffix>.sh), e.g. "-pre" / "-post".

review_by.description: Sunset-review date, YYYY-MM-DD (#1300). Optional per ENTRY, required per hook NAME by check-plugin-manifests.py rule 26: the first registration carries it and multi-event siblings may omit it, mirroring `hosts`. Defaults to merge date + 90 days; a past date fails the check until the hook is re-audited (bump the date or record the verdict in docs/hook-prune-audit.md). Never copied into a platform hooks.json.

hosts.description: Host whitelist; absent means all hosts. Values are host_id values from manifests/platforms/*.json — extend this enum when adding a platform.

requires.description: External components without which the matcher is dead (#1158); mirrored by the spec's Requires: line.

gates.description: Named command families this entry gates (e.g. git-commit); consumed by scripts/check-sibling-commit-gates.py.

mode.description: Operating-surface metadata (#688): the single source of truth cross-checked against docs/bypass-vars.md and SECURITY.md.

strict_env.description: Env var that switches the hook from advisory to blocking. Deliberately a bare string (not an array like its siblings) — that is the shape every consumer reads today; widening it to an array is a semantic change tracked outside this schema.

observe_only.description: True for a hook that by design never escalates — it records and exits 0, with no advise/ask/deny path. Exempts the hook from the zero-escalation Investigate rule at sunset review (#1300; CONTRIBUTING.md → Evidence and sunset review).
